rounds.text: The business is experiencing an explosive inflection in profitability, evidenced by compounded profit growth of 194% over the trailing twelve months and 70% over three years [E21, E20]. This phenomenal earnings momentum is starkly outpacing historical share price growth, creating a classic fundamentals-led divergence where profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 207% [E46]. Furthermore, operating cash flow robustly supports these bottom-line gains, demonstrating an exceptional cash conversion rate of 3.00x where profits are fully backed by actual cash [E34]. Operational acceleration is further highlighted by a strong trailing twelve-month sales growth of 20% [E17] alongside positive screening indicators flagging strong YoY sales growth of 48% and net profit soaring by 183% [E56, E58]. Finally, the company is explicitly expected to deliver a good upcoming quarter [E48], signalling that current market sentiment and stale pricing have yet to catch up to this accelerating operational turnaround [E63]. Conceded: [E42].

Fine Line Circuits Ltd trades at an alarming P/E of 78.1x on filed statements [E1], which stretches even higher to 258.8x according to key ratios against a sector benchmark of just 20.84x [E6]. This excessive valuation is completely disconnected from the company's persistently weak profitability metrics, highlighted by a low 3-year median return on equity of 3% [E28] and an anemic ROCE of 5.6% [E12] that lags far behind the sector benchmark of 11.69% [E10]. Furthermore, fundamental value is severely undermined by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 15 per share against a market price of Rs 86.1, leaving a staggering negative margin of safety of -491.4% [E42, E43]. Compounded sales growth over the past decade sits at a sluggish 3% [E14], accompanied by a negative one-year share price return of -13% [E25] and substantial contingent liabilities of Rs 66.9 Cr [E54]. Meanwhile, borrowings have increased to Rs 7.47 Cr alongside negative free cash flow of Rs -1.45 Cr in March 2026 [E36, E38], while low promoter holding at 33.4% limits inside alignment [E52]. Conceded: compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months reached 194% and cash conversion stood at a strong 3.00x [E21, E34].

The bear points to high P/E multiples of 78.1x and 258.8x [E1, E6], but ignores that fundamental growth has radically broken away from historical trends, with trailing twelve-month profit growth surging 194% [E21] and upcoming performance flagged to deliver a good quarter [E48]. Conceded: the DCF model indicates intrinsic value at Rs 15 against a market price of Rs 86.1 [E42]. However, dismissing the stock on stale sentiment misses a major turnaround where results score 98 out of 100 and recent profit growth outperforms 1-year price growth by 207% [E46, E63]. While the bear highlights an anemic ROCE of 5.6% and a 3-year median ROE of 3% [E12, E28], it glosses over the robust cash conversion of 3.00x where profits are fully backed by operating cash [E34]. Furthermore, the bear cites a sluggish 10-year sales growth of 3% [E14] while overlooking acceleration to 20% in the trailing twelve months and a 48% year-on-year sales jump [E17, E56]. Finally, the bear flags a 1-year share price return of -13% [E25], whereas the fundamentals-led signal explicitly shows that profits are outpacing the stock price [E45].
